history.summary: PROVISIONAL IDENTIFICATION: the CSV row 'Mokokchung Vishnu Temple' has no dedicated web page. The best-supported referent is the 'Bishnu Mandir' listed among the Hindu temples of Mokokchung on onefivenine.com (Mokokchung, Nagaland 798601, about 1.4 km from the town centre); 'Bishnu' is the regional spelling of 'Vishnu', so this is plausibly the Vishnu temple the CSV intends. No further details - no address, photos, founding date or visiting information - could be found for this shrine. Mokokchung is overwhelmingly Baptist Christian (about 95% per travel guides), so Hindu shrines here are small community temples, mostly serving the Gorkha and other non-Naga communities. Coordinates are the geocoded Mokokchung town centroid, provisional. Treat as an unverified directory-listing record; field verification recommended.

town_description: Mokokchung is the district headquarters of Mokokchung district in Nagaland, set at about 1,325 m altitude, and is known as the cultural and intellectual capital of the state. It is the homeland of the Ao Naga tribe, who introduced Christianity to the region in the 19th century; around 95% of the district's population is Baptist Christian. The main Ao festivals are Moatsu (sowing, early May) and Tsungremmong (harvest, August).
